discovery: Development of matter-wave interferometry with atoms and its use as a precision probe of gravity, inertia and fundamental constants

nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique des Lasers, Université Sorbonne Paris Nord / CNRS, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Atom interferometry turned the de Broglie wave of a neutral atom into a measuring instrument of extraordinary sensitivity. Bordé showed that laser-driven transitions act as coherent beam splitters for atoms (the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer). Pritchard realized atom interferometry with material gratings and pioneered precision measurements of atomic properties and decoherence. Kasevich invented the light-pulse atom interferometer using stimulated Raman transitions, creating gravimeters, gradiometers and gyroscopes of unprecedented accuracy. These instruments now measure the Newtonian constant G and the fine-structure constant, test the equivalence principle at the 10^-12 level, probe gravitational effects across metre-scale wavepacket separations, and are deployed in geodesy and navigation. Like optical clocks, they connect quantum control of atoms with relativity and geoscience, removing classical limits through elegant physics and painstaking error budgets. This is a mature, transformative body of work whose originators deserve recognition.
